window.label: annualised estimate = supplier total in window x 12 / months

limitations: Spend dates are payment-run timestamps, not invoice or transaction dates; the 30-day and 7-day windows are measured on payment-run dates.
Rows with supplier 'Redacted' cannot be tested by supplier; they are excluded and reported by Expenditure category and tag.
Only 3 months of data, so the x4 annualisation is an estimate (annualised estimate).
The Contracts Finder notice export holds only contracts above about 25,000 GBP; absence of a notice for a smaller supplier is expected and is never a finding.
Tags are a heuristic on published fields (Narrative, Expenditure category, Service, supplier text), not a classification of the underlying contract.
Supplier matching between spend and notices is by normalised name only; the spend data carries no Companies House number. Candidates are never counted as matches.
The spend data has no transaction id; identical rows are kept and treated as possible duplicates, never confirmed ones.
Redacted-supplier, pension/statutory, internal and other public-body rows are outside the supplier tests; public-body review list and exclusion pairs are provided for the auditor to confirm.

Boundary treatment follows the PDF wording as stored in rules.json: the 500,000 GBP boundary is exclusive on both sides (CPR-62 high, CPR-64 low), so a payment or total of exactly 500,000 does not reach that tier and is not flagged by the 500,000 tests.
The 1,000 GBP lower bound is stored as exclusive (CPR-59), so a total must exceed 1,000 to reach that tier; amounts of exactly 1,000 are not treated as reaching it.
Auditor decisions pending, nothing excluded: public_body_review.csv (101 names) and exclusion_pairs.csv (5 pairs) remain in the analysed population for the auditor to review.

cleaning.supplier_normalisation: uppercase; & -> AND; apostrophes deleted; other punctuation -> space; drop LTD/LIMITED/PLC/LLP; collapse whitespace

tagging.method: heuristic on published fields; first match wins in order grant > care_or_education_placement > agency_staff > premises > general_procurement

grant.rationale: Narrative says grant. Rules 1.6.2 treat a grant as a contract, so grants stay in scope.

care_or_education_placement.rationale: Placement/care allowances/direct payments by narrative, and contractor payments inside social-care or education services. Appendix C row F excludes some individual care placements from competition, so a flag here may be lawfully outside competition.

agency_staff.rationale: Narrative or supplier text indicating agency or temporary staffing.

premises.rationale: Expenditure category Premises, plus rents, repairs and maintenance, cleaning, grounds maintenance and minor works narratives.

general_procurement.rationale: Default for everything else; ambiguous narratives listed in tagging.unmapped_review.

tagging.unmapped_review_note: top 20 narratives by GBP left in general_procurement, for auditor review

date_warnings.issue: end date more than max plausible years after window

matching.method: exact = identical normalised name; candidates (difflib>=0.85, token containment with >=2 tokens in the smaller name, trading-as part) are never counted as matches

threshold_clustering@1000.interpretation: Payments just below 1,000 GBP (within 10 percent) may indicate amounts shaped to stay under a procurement route boundary; the adjacent lower band is shown for context so the auditor can judge whether the concentration is unusual. Innocent explanations include fixed or tariff prices, standard rates for recurring care or service charges, and round-number pricing. Worth confirming against quotes or tender records. Care placements may be lawfully outside competition (Appendix C row F, CPR-72).

split_purchases@1000.interpretation: Several payments to one supplier close together whose combined value reaches 1,000 GBP may indicate a requirement split into smaller purchases (anti-avoidance rule CPR-13), consistent with a pattern worth confirming. Innocent explanations: regular recurring payments (common for care packages and rents, see all_amounts_equal), separate unrelated orders, or one contract invoiced in instalments. Spend dates are payment-run timestamps, not invoice dates, so windows are measured on payment-run dates. Windows are anchored greedily so each payment sits in one group per tier.

duplicates.interpretation: Repeated same-amount payments to one supplier within 7 days are possible duplicate payments to investigate, not confirmed ones. Groups identical on every published field are flagged separately; with no transaction id they may still be separate legitimate payments (for example several invoices of the same value, or weekly or per-person care charges). Spend dates are payment-run timestamps, not invoice dates, so windows are measured on payment-run dates.

off_contract.interpretation: Suppliers above the notice threshold with no exact-name council notice may indicate spend without a published contract; worth confirming. The Contracts Finder export holds only contracts above about 25,000 GBP, so this test never questions suppliers below the threshold. Innocent explanations: care placements and other individual placements (possibly lawfully outside competition, Appendix C row F), framework or DPS call-offs, other public-sector bodies, notices published under a different or group name (see candidate_notice, never counted as matches), contracts awarded before 2021 or not published, grants, or utilities. Disjoint from expired_notice_spend.

parameters.condition: every exact-matching notice has a contract end date before the window start; blank end date counts as active

expired_notice_spend.interpretation: Suppliers paid in the window whose every matching notice ended before it began may indicate spend after contract expiry without an approved extension (Appendix C row D, CPR-69); worth confirming. Innocent explanations: a newer contract or extension not published as a notice, an approved extension recorded only in council records, call-off from a framework, or a name-only match to a different entity. Matching is by name only. Disjoint from off_contract.

parameters.condition: supplier has exactly one active exact-match notice, single-supplier, Awarded Value > 0

spend_vs_award.interpretation: Annualised spend at or above 1.25 times the annual equivalent of the award may indicate spend beyond the award without an approved variation (Appendix C row E, CPR-70, CPR-71); worth confirming. Innocent explanations: Awarded Value is often an estimate or a minimum rather than a cap, payments may include other contracts with the same supplier, lumpy or front-loaded payment profiles in a three-month window, or a variation approved in council records. Name-only matching.
